name: Sandhar Technologies Ltd
title: Sandhar Technologies Ltd - 541163 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Sandhar guides 15%+ FY27 revenue growth excluding price re-trigger, capex 5-7% of revenue (INR 275-310 cr), but margins flat-ish: +0.25% EBITDA target, with aluminium pass-through lag and April manpower shock dragging near term.

summary.headline: Sandhar FY26 consolidated revenue INR 4,852 crore (+25%), EBITDA INR 513 crore (10.6% margin); FY27 guided to grow over 15% before any price re-trigger.
summary.overview: FY26 was a record year: consolidated revenue rose 25% to INR 4,852 crore, EBITDA rose 28% to INR 513 crore at a 10.6% margin, and PAT rose 40% to INR 199 crore. Q4 consolidated revenue grew 29% YoY with an 11% EBITDA margin, and the India business grew 28% in FY26. Overseas subsidiaries swung to break-even at EBT in Q4 after a FY26 loss of EUR 2.56 million, though aluminium pass-through lags are expected to weigh on Q1 FY27. Management cited April manpower absenteeism and raw material shortages as the main near-term disruption, with May reported as better than April.

financial_highlights.metric: Consolidated Q4 revenue and EBITDA margin

financial_highlights.value: Revenue INR 257 crore, EBITDA INR 28.25 crore

financial_highlights.change: Q4 EBITDA margin 14.6%, EBT about break-even
Working capital debt INR 564 crore; term loans INR 384 crore

segments.name: India business
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR 4,384 crore (+28%), EBITDA INR 472 crore (+32%). Management said industry grew 12.7% while Sandhar India grew 28%; two-wheeler business grew 35.1% vs industry 12.9%.

segments.name: Overseas subsidiaries
segments.commentary: FY26 loss of EUR 2.56 million; Q4 EBITDA margin 14.6% and EBT roughly break-even. Revenue of about EUR 46 million with full-year decline of about 8.5% in euro terms, per analyst. Pass-through lag of about 180 days in overseas contracts.

segments.name: Joint ventures
segments.commentary: Five JVs generated revenue of INR 257 crore and EBITDA of INR 28.25 crore in FY26; Sandhar investment about INR 62 crore.

segments.name: EV business
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue about INR 20 crore; 41,000 battery chargers and 5,500 motor control units sold. Targeted to double in FY27; EBT turnaround expected in FY28.

segments.name: New projects (Sundaram-Clayton die-casting, Khed City, Sanaswadi cabins/fabrication)
segments.commentary: INR 342 crore invested to generate INR 468 crore revenue in FY26; Sundaram-Clayton FY26 revenue INR 369 crore. Management expects about 2x-2.5x revenue (about INR 750 crore) in FY27. Turnaround timelines: Khed City and Sanaswadi from Q2 FY27, Sundaram-Clayton from Q3 FY27 (still EBT losses for FY27).

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue growth guided at over 15% (15-16%), excluding a likely price re-trigger on input cost increases.
EBITDA margin expected to improve by about 0.25% in FY27 for existing businesses; new projects will dilute, with 1.5-2 years to profitability.
Management targets doubling revenue every three to four years, with a stated post-tax ROCE target of 15%, peaking at 20%; at INR 10,000 crore revenue, PAT of about INR 450 crore was cited.
FY27 capex estimated at INR 275-310 crore (5-7% of revenue), covering growth, maintenance and upgradation.
Overseas business expected to return to planned levels once aluminium pass-through lag clears; Romania targeted for break-even in FY28.
Manpower availability expected to normalise by end-June 2026 per management, with May better than April.
capex_capacity: Capital work in progress closing balance INR 104-115 crore (figure cited differently on call); mostly expected to capitalise by end of Q2 FY27 as Sundaram-Clayton relocation, Khed City and Sanaswadi projects complete.
Sundaram-Clayton die-casting business shifting to own premises, targeted by end of Q2 FY27.
FY27 capex outlay of INR 275-310 crore expected.

Technology: telematics and smart-key products presented to customers; POCs next, development in FY27, production thereafter. Partnering on royalty-based technology transfer, not JVs; target to take to market within 12 months.
Smart Key locksets at about 5,000 per month and growing.
demand_pricing: Management said domestic auto demand is strong, but manpower constraints limit industry output; absenteeism reached around 20% at one point in April, and state minimum wages rose 30-40%.
Two-wheeler inventory at some customers fell from about 60 days to under 14 days; industry lost an estimated 200,000-300,000 vehicles.

Aluminium and gas costs rose sharply in March-April; India pass-through lag is about three months (aiming for 30 days), and overseas lag about 180 days (aiming for 90 days). Pass-through from June expected to recover April costs.
Price re-trigger expected across the industry as input costs rise; not included in the 15% growth guidance.
Working capital: overseas inventory holding about 54-55 days vs about 12-13 days in India.

qa_highlights.question: How will the planned doubling of revenue every 3-4 years be achieved, and which segments drive it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited two-wheelers, new businesses in sheet metal and casting, and proprietary products like locks and mirrors; it said a 15-16% growth guide is conservative and excludes the price re-trigger.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for the new projects and their profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: INR 342 crore invested generated INR 468 crore in FY26 and is expected to reach about INR 750 crore in FY27; Khed City and Sanaswadi turn around in Q2 FY27, Sundaram-Clayton in Q3 with EBT losses for FY27, EV and Romania in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA margins improve and by how much?
qa_highlights.answer: Existing businesses are targeted to gain about 0.25% in EBITDA margin in FY27; new projects will dilute margins until they mature, with 1.5-2 years to turnaround.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt position and debt-to-equity trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross debt INR 948 crore, of which INR 564 crore is working capital debt; term loans INR 384 crore with about INR 103 crore repayable this year. Management called the debt-to-equity ratio healthy versus peers.

qa_highlights.question: Why did overseas borrowings rise in INR terms despite a small euro increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Bill discounting was reclassified to borrowings under Ind AS, and INR translation at the closing rate (about INR 111 per euro vs INR 108 in March) inflated the INR figure; the euro increase was about EUR 5 million.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company keep the overseas business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the overseas presence supports Indian customer relationships; it will revisit the business after the year but gave no decision.

qa_highlights.question: What is the company's competitive advantage in castings?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited integrated capability across high- and low-pressure die casting, machining, zinc, magnesium and aluminium castings, from small to very large parts including engine blocks.

risks_watch: Aluminium and gas cost pass-through lags of three months in India and about 180 days overseas, which will hit Q1 FY27 margins.
Manpower shortages and wage hikes in several states could keep volumes below demand; management expects normalisation by end-June 2026.
New project losses (Sundaram-Clayton, EV, Romania) in FY27 could slow the margin improvement.
Working capital intensity: receivable days at 44 (consolidated) and inventory days at 54-55 for overseas operations; overseas debt in INR rose partly due to reclassification.
Price re-trigger not yet secured; the FY27 growth guidance excludes it.
Overseas business strategy unresolved; management will revisit after the year.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on demand and FY27 growth, while flagging near-term cost, manpower and pass-through lag headwinds. Management was conservative on guidance and deferred on overseas strategy and some numbers, and several answers were reconciled on the call.
key_quotes: So, even on a conservative level, I am happy to give a guidance of over a 15% growth in the overall revenue.
Sandhar has crossed the revenue mark of over INR 4,800 crores, which is an all-time high.

So, while EBITDA levels will remain constant around 11%, but with the volumes coming up and the revenue going up, automatically in terms of absolute returns, our multiplier will be giving us a more return on capital employed.
We are not looking at joint ventures at this time. We are considering transfer of technology or collaborations, which will be on the royalty basis.

adds.what: Sundaram-Clayton die-casting business relocation to own premises

growth.why: FY27 consolidated revenue growth guided at over 15% (15-16%) excluding a possible price re-trigger, backed by new projects expected to rise 2-2.5x to about INR 750 crore, Sundaram-Clayton and Khed/Sanaswadi commissioning in Q2-Q3 FY27, and a 0.25% EBITDA margin improvement; the 15% figure lacks a full order-book or capacity bridge, so backing is partial.
